source_refs.note: Exercise 14.4 Q1 (i)-(iii), book p.289 (PDF 294). Answer key PDF 312: 25, 14, 10 cubic units, all correct (sympy). Solution book PDF 1266-1268 agrees.

blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the volume of parallelepiped for which the given vectors are three edges: \(\underline{u} = 3\underline{i} + 2\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = -\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
A volume question: the three vectors are the edges of a box (parallelepiped) from one corner.
We must find its volume.
Plan: volume \(= |[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}]|\); write the components as a 3 by 3 determinant and expand it.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = 3\underline{i} + 2\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = -\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\).
To find: the volume \(V\) of the parallelepiped with edges \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}, \underline{w}\).
Method: \(V = |\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} \times \underline{w})|\) (14.4.2). In components the scalar triple product is the determinant of the three rows of components (14.4.4).

Write the components as rows
\[[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}] = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 is \(\underline{u}\), row 2 is \(\underline{v}\), row 3 is \(\underline{w}\). A missing unit vector means a 0 component.

Expand along row 1
\[= 3\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[\quad - 0\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[\quad + 2\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 3(8 + 1) - 0 + 2(-1 - 0)\]
\[= 27 - 2 = 25\]
Why: Each entry of row 1 times its minor (the 2 by 2 determinant left after covering its row and column), with signs \(+, -, +\).

Take the absolute value
\[V = |25| = 25\]
Why: A volume is never negative; here the triple product is already positive.

Check: expand down column 1 instead
\[3(8 + 1) - 1(0 \cdot 4 - 2 \cdot (-1)) + 0\]
\[= 27 - 2 = 25 \;\checkmark\]
Why: A determinant has the same value whichever row or column we expand along.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the volume of parallelepiped for which the given vectors are three edges: \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} - 4\underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} - \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
A volume question: the three vectors are the edges of a box (parallelepiped) from one corner.
We must find its volume.
Plan: volume \(= |[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}]|\); write the components as a 3 by 3 determinant and expand it.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} - 4\underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} - \underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
To find: the volume \(V\) of the parallelepiped with edges \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}, \underline{w}\).
Method: \(V = |\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} \times \underline{w})|\) (14.4.2). In components the scalar triple product is the determinant of the three rows of components (14.4.4).

Write the components as rows
\[[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}] = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -4 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 2 & -3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 is \(\underline{u}\), row 2 is \(\underline{v}\), row 3 is \(\underline{w}\). A missing unit vector means a 0 component.

Expand along row 1
\[= 1\begin{vmatrix} -1 & -2 \\ -3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[\quad + 4\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[\quad - 1\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & -3 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-1 - 6) + 4(1 + 4) - 1(-3 + 2)\]
\[= -7 + 20 + 1 = 14\]
Why: Each entry of row 1 times its minor (the 2 by 2 determinant left after covering its row and column), with signs \(+, -, +\).

Take the absolute value
\[V = |14| = 14\]
Why: A volume is never negative; here the triple product is already positive.

Check: find \(\underline{v} \times \underline{w}\) first, then dot with \(\underline{u}\)
\[\underline{v} \times \underline{w} = -7\underline{i} - 5\underline{j} - \underline{k}\]
\[\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} \times \underline{w}) = -7 + 20 + 1\]
\[= 14 \;\checkmark\]
Why: This is the definition \(\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} \times \underline{w})\) worked the long way; it agrees with the determinant.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Find the volume of parallelepiped for which the given vectors are three edges: \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = 2\underline{i} - \underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = \underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
A volume question: the three vectors are the edges of a box (parallelepiped) from one corner.
We must find its volume.
Plan: volume \(= |[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}]|\); write the components as a 3 by 3 determinant and expand it.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = 2\underline{i} - \underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = \underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
To find: the volume \(V\) of the parallelepiped with edges \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}, \underline{w}\).
Method: \(V = |\underline{u} \cdot (\underline{v} \times \underline{w})|\) (14.4.2). In components the scalar triple product is the determinant of the three rows of components (14.4.4).

Write the components as rows
\[[\underline{u}\ \underline{v}\ \underline{w}] = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 is \(\underline{u}\), row 2 is \(\underline{v}\), row 3 is \(\underline{w}\). A missing unit vector means a 0 component.

Expand along row 1
\[= 1\begin{vmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[\quad + 2\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[\quad + 3\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-1 + 1) + 2(2 - 0) + 3(2 - 0)\]
\[= 0 + 4 + 6 = 10\]
Why: Each entry of row 1 times its minor (the 2 by 2 determinant left after covering its row and column), with signs \(+, -, +\).

Take the absolute value
\[V = |10| = 10\]
Why: A volume is never negative; here the triple product is already positive.

Check: expand down column 1
\[1(-1 + 1) - 2((-2)(1) - 3(1)) + 0\]
\[= 0 - 2(-5) = 10 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Column 1 has a 0, so this expansion is short and gives the same value.
